subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical exec approval inputs, and must that cache be per reviewer/run with the full reviewed input as its key?
rationale: The source-reproduced cost bug is narrow, but caching an exec reviewer result changes when a later request bypasses a fresh model review, so cache lifetime and key shape need owner intent before automation changes the approval boundary.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or rendered prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approvals.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once decisions and keep ask, error, and timeout outcomes fresh for a narrower behavior change with less savings.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or billing evidence justifies a cache.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or rendered prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This user authored the merged normalized auto mode PR that introduced the affected model-backed exec auto-review behavior and documented its approval semantics.
